name: cut_list_counts_the_bars
why: ENTRY Z-C6. `cut_list` has been in the catalogue with `Provata = true` forever, and until 23/9/2026 **no bench run touched it**: not a declared case, not the bench's C#, not a hand-made plan. «Provata» there meant «someone measured it once», not «something checks it every time» — and the two things read the same in the file.
_why_it_counts: It is the document you go to the workshop with, and it is the reason a frame is made with structural members instead of extrusions. A cut list that counts the wrong bars sends the wrong iron to be cut, and gives no error.
defect_caught: **AND ON 26/9/2026 IT CAUGHT ONE THAT HAD SLIPPED THROUGH (entry GT2).** The case was green with the WRONG cut list: a single item, «QUANTITY 4, LENGTH 1000» — four bars of 1000 where two are 800. It counted the bodies, and the bodies were right. Now it asks for the items too: two, one of 1000 and one of 800, four bars in all. Then: a cut list that is born empty, or that counts a different number of bars from those there are. `bodies_in_cut_list` is read by ASKING the folders of the cut list how many bodies they have — not by copying the number of the part's bodies — so the two numbers can diverge, and it is exactly when they diverge that you need to know it.

expect.why: four bars: it is the number the cut list is compared with two steps below. Without this line, «the cut list counts four» would be true even on a badly built frame

expect._and_this_is_the_comparison: **THE TWO NUMBERS COME FROM TWO DIFFERENT PLACES.** `bodies` is counted by the state of the part; `bodies_in_cut_list` is asked of the folders of the cut list, one by one. They are equal when the cut list is right, and when they diverge it is exactly the moment when someone would go to the workshop with the wrong sheet.
expect.why: four bars in the part, four items in the cut list
the cut list was BORN in this step, not found already made: without this line the case would be green even if the operation had done nothing and had just read a pre-existing cut list
two lengths, two items: with the cut list from before it was 1, and the case did not see it
the lengths READ from the properties of the items (the LENGTH@@@ expression), not recomputed: 1000 and 800, like the frame asked for
the sum of the quantities of the items is the number of bars: two plus two

the rectangular_frame does not put in the «Saldatura» feature (the Italian SOLIDWORKS name of the weldment feature): it is this step that makes the part a weldment, and it is the reason the items are separated
